transcript: A real book store is the venue for this Pulitzer winning play performed by a pair of acclaimed film and TV stars who are married in real life. And the tickets are somehow only $20. Two time Oscar nominee Debra Winger and Arliss Howard star in this intimate revival of the Gin Game, performed in the Housing Works bookstore in Soho, where my fave Taylor Swift shot All Too Well, the short film. This 1976 play is about two lonely people in a senior living facility attempting to find solace in a shared game of gin. But tempers rise as the card game begins to feel like a stand in for much more. And it's kind of wild to see actors of this caliber perform this play in such an intimate setting. As for the play itself, this was actually my first exposure to it and I had kinda mixed feelings about it. On one hand, it has really good scene work and character work, and it's this aching portrait of people estranged from their families late in life, desperate for connection. And the repetitive structure of the play is a reflection of that; She keeps coming back to play with him even though he gets really nasty and belligerent. But that also makes it a frustrating watch. Like, the extremity of his outburst combined with the repetition for me, started to strain believability, even though we know intellectually why they do what they do. Maybe the play has aged badly in the sense that, I don't know, people nowadays don't have the same patience for petulant outbursts from grown men. I don't know. Aside from the remarkable sense of intimacy, I don't know that being performed in a bookstore had much of an effect on the experience for me. But it was a fun novelty, and they definitely made the space work. And even with my reservations, it's hard not to recommend taking the opportunity to see this classic play performed by these actors at this price point and this level of intimacy.
classificationReason: Creator personally attended this revival of The Gin Game (Debra Winger and Arliss Howard at Housing Works bookstore) and shares a first-hand opinion with clear pros/cons. Matches 'the-gin-game-2026' on the list.
